newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Two chase presidency in Moldova's rebel Dnestr.
newsitem.headline: Two chase presidency in Moldova's rebel Dnestr.

text.p: Two candidates will run for president in elections Moldova's rebel Dnestr region will hold on December 22, in defiance of the rest of the country which chooses a new president on November 17.

Dnestr, a heavily industrialised 700,000-strong area in Moldova's east, broke away in 1990 on fears its mostly Slav residents could be sidelined in Moldova's eventual merger with ethnic kin in neighbouring Romania.

Dnestr's central electoral commission announced late on Saturday the two candidates would be the current leader Igor Smirnov, 55, elected Dnestr president on December 1, 1991, and Vladimir Malakhov, 44, a local official.
Smirnov, a Soviet-era industrial manager, used to run one of the region's biggest factories. He is viewed as the sure winner of the future poll.

"Most probably, the second candidate is running just for the sake of appearances to show there is some democracy in this quasi-state...But in any case, Malakhov propagates the same separatist theories as Smirnov," a local reporter said.
Moldova's talks with Dnestr leaders over the rebel region's future status are stalemated over separatist demands for full independence. Moldova is offering broad autonomy.
Hundreds were killed in a bloody war between Moldovan security forces and Dnestr separatists in 1992.

Top separatists have said they will not allow polling stations on their territory when Moldova elects its official president on November 17, but have promised to let local residents go and vote freely outside the region.
